questions.question: Dr. Sami receives a patient who insults him. Dr. Mina advises him to stay calm. What is the best conflict management technique in the practice?
options: Active listening and reformulation to defuse anger
Respond in the same tone to show authority
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Active listening and reformulation allow defusing anger by showing you understand their emotion.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will try to reformulate their anger.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina trains a young assistant in patient reception. What is the fundamental principle of the first contact with an anxious patient?
options: Establish eye contact and a kind smile
Speak quickly to not waste time
Stay behind the desk to maintain professional distance
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Eye contact and a kind smile immediately create a climate of trust.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will train my team in kind reception.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient who always cancels appointments at the last minute. Dr. Mina advises him to explore the reason. What is the most frequent cause of cancellations?
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Dental anxiety is the most frequent cause of repeated cancellations.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will contact my patient to understand.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina uses the 'STOP' technique with a panicked patient. What technique is this?
options: A breathing technique where you inhale, hold, then exhale slowly
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The STOP technique (Stop, Take a breath, Observe, Proceed) is a breathing method to calm anxiety.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will learn this technique.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami must deliver bad news (treatment failure). Dr. Mina advises him to use the SPIKES protocol. What does SPIKES mean?
options: A 6-step protocol for delivering bad news: Setting, Perception, Invitation, Knowledge, Emotions, Strategy
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The SPIKES protocol is a structured method for delivering bad news with empathy.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will follow this protocol.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina observes that a patient systematically avoids eye contact. She concludes that...
options: The patient is probably anxious or has a social disorder
The patient does not trust her skills
The patient does not want to be treated
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Avoiding eye contact is often a sign of anxiety or social disorder.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will adapt my communication with this patient.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient who asks very technical questions. Dr. Mina advises him to...
options: Answer precisely using adapted language and analogies
Avoid answering because it's too technical
Tell them it's not their role to understand
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Technical questions are a form of active participation in their care.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will take the time to explain properly.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina uses metaphors to explain treatments to children. Why is this technique effective?
options: Metaphors make abstract concepts concrete and understandable for children
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Metaphors help children visualize and understand procedures.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will prepare metaphors for children.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami notices that a patient has a defensive posture (crossed arms, turned body). Dr. Mina tells him this probably means...
options: A protective posture in the face of a situation perceived as threatening
A simple habit of the patient
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Crossed arms and a turned body are signs of protection and discomfort.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will try to put them at ease.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina trains her team in 'positive language.' What is the rule of positive language in patient communication?
options: Formulate sentences positively ('I will anesthetize you gently' rather than 'It will hurt')
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Positive language reduces anxiety by focusing on pleasant sensations.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will reformulate all my sentences.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient who cries in the chair. Dr. Mina advises him to...
options: Offer a tissue, give them time, and acknowledge their emotion
Continue treatment as if nothing happened
Call a colleague to replace him
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Tears are an emotional expression to be welcomed with kindness.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will give them time to calm down.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina uses the reframing technique with an anxious patient. What is reframing?
options: Changing the patient's perspective so they see the situation in a more positive light
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Reframing allows transforming a situation perceived as negative into an opportunity.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will help my patient see treatment differently.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient with a fear of the dental handpiece. Dr. Mina advises him to...
options: Let them hear the handpiece sound from a distance, then gradually get closer
Not use the handpiece at all
Tell them the sound isn't important
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Gradual desensitization is effective for fear of noises.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will offer a gradual approach.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina must prepare a patient for anesthesia. She uses the 'tell-show-do' technique. What does this technique mean?
options: Explain (Tell), show (Show), do (Do): a 3-step education method
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Tell-Show-Do is a validated technique for preparing children for treatments.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will use it with all my anxious patients.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient who talks constantly during treatment. Dr. Mina advises him to...
options: Use speech as a distraction tool while guiding them towards moments of silence
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Speech can be a beneficial distraction, but moments of silence are needed for concentration.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will channel their speech.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina trains an intern in managing patients in crisis. What is the priority in case of a panic attack?
options: Secure the patient and bring them back to reality with grounding techniques
Leave them alone to calm down
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Grounding allows bringing the patient back to reality and reducing panic.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will learn grounding techniques.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami receives a patient who criticizes his work. Dr. Mina advises him not to take criticism personally. How to handle patient criticism?
options: Welcome the criticism, reformulate, and propose a solution
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Criticism is feedback to be welcomed with professionalism.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will listen and propose solutions.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina has a patient with a communication disorder (aphasia). What strategy should she adopt?
options: Use visual aids, closed-ended questions, and plenty of patience
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Visual aids and closed-ended questions facilitate communication with aphasic patients.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will prepare visual cards.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient with a fear of dentists since childhood. Dr. Mina tells him it's a learned phobia. How is a learned phobia treated?
options: Through a cognitive-behavioral approach combined with gradual exposure
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Learned phobias are treated through a cognitive and behavioral approach.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will refer my patient to a CBT psychologist.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina explains to Dr. Sami the concept of 'compassion fatigue.' What is compassion fatigue?
options: Emotional exhaustion related to excessive empathy towards patients
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Compassion fatigue affects empathetic caregivers who invest too much emotionally.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will watch my emotional balance.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient who refuses to keep follow-up appointments. Dr. Mina advises him to...
options: Explain the importance of follow-up with clear arguments and concrete benefits
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Patient motivation comes from understanding the benefits of follow-up.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will explain the importance of check-ups.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina uses the grounding technique with a panicked patient. What is an effective grounding technique?
options: Ask the patient to name 5 things they see, 4 they touch, 3 they hear
Talk to them about their problems
Ask them to close their eyes
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Sensory grounding brings the patient to the present moment and reduces panic.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will use the 5-4-3-2-1 technique.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami has a patient who expresses a lot of negative emotions. Dr. Mina advises him to...
options: Welcome the emotions, name them, and validate them without judgment
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Validating emotions is a key skill for building trust.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will name their emotions to defuse them.'

questions.question: Dr. Mina teaches Dr. Sami the importance of 'presence' in consultation. What does it mean to be 'present' with a patient?
options: Be fully attentive, without distraction, focusing on the patient
Be physically present but thinking about something else
Look at your phone during the consultation
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Authentic presence is the basis of a quality care relationship.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will put my phone away during consultations.'

questions.question: Dr. Sami, after having mastered relational techniques with Dr. Mina, receives her congratulations. What is the next step for Dr. Sami?
options: Become an expert in helping relationships and caregiver-patient communication
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Mastery of the caregiver-patient relationship is a valuable skill. Becoming an expert is the next step.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will train in helping relationships.'
